target_customer: Developers and companies wanting a social network on Rails
problem: Building a social network from scratch was slow, and hosted builders such as Ning were closed.
business_model: Open source MIT licensed platform with consulting and hosting (not confirmed)

founders.name: Michael Hartl
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch April 2008: author of RailsSpace. YC page: later wrote Rails Tutorial and founded Softcover (acquired May 2022).

founders.name: Long Nguyen
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page; a GitHub mirror also names him as co-developer.

competitors.name: Ning
competitors.what: Do it yourself hosted social network builder
competitors.traction_then: Most publicized in the category per TechCrunch

competitors.name: Lovd By Less
competitors.what: Rails social network that appeared to be open sourced earlier

technical_complexity.rationale: A full Rails social network codebase with standard features, mostly engineering effort.

defensibility.rationale: MIT licensed code can be forked by anyone and rivals were also open source.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer found; the GitHub repository says development was frozen in 2010.

market_need_then: Interest in owning a social network was shown by Ning and by Hartl's RailsSpace book.

brand_strength.rationale: No brand sources apart from the launch press; name origin not stated.

outcome_analysis: Insoshi released an MIT licensed Rails social network at YC W08 and presented at Spring 2008 demo day. With a free copyable codebase and only about $20K of known funding, it found no commercial path and the main repository froze in 2010. The YC page calls the project defunct, but no shutdown account exists, so the failure factors are inferred.
notes: insoshi.com redirects (301) to namarne.com, which was not fetched because the redirect is cross host and unrelated. The $20K total rests on a single database (CB Insights) with no date; 2008 is assumed from YC batch year and recorded as such. Failure factors inferred. Exit unknown because no shutdown notice found.
